SECTION 1

* A 24-year-old writer is frustrated that older people criticize young people for spending money on holidays or dining out instead of saving for a house, when in reality housing has become unaffordable for their generation.

* The writer believes that due to high property prices, limited housing availability, and banks being unwilling to lend money, many young people will never be able to own a home and will rent forever.

* A second writer points out that workers under 25 years old are legally paid less than older workers for doing the exact same job, which makes saving money even harder.

* Young workers aged 21-24 can be paid as little as £7.05 per hour (compared to the higher "national living wage" for over-25s), and 18-20 year olds can earn as little as £5.60 per hour.

* Young people are more likely to have unstable zero-hours contracts and low annual incomes (around £14,500), making it nearly impossible to save enough money to buy property while also covering basic living expenses.
